We start a new sermon series this Sunday at our 11AM Worship Gathering in Bowman Hall 133! Hereâs a description of the series: 

We have domesticated Jesus. Weâve made him into whatever suits our desires. He exists to guarantee my happiness in this life. He makes my life easy. We ask: âWhy wouldnât everyone follow him?â Then we stumble on some things he said. Some really harsh and demanding things. Things that mess with our expectations, that shatter our âthis is easyâ view of Christianity. We see him systematically turn our definitions and boundaries of faith upside down. We scramble to explain them away. We donât sit with the shock and the scandal of his words. But there is a cost to the choice of ignoring them. Our Jesus is too tame. Our faith never makes us uncomfortable.Â What does it look like to be uncomfortable in your season of life? We perhaps deem what is uncomfortable in life as âbadâ or âwrongâ. In light of Jesus and His commands, we need to get comfortable being uncomfortable. In serving each other, in outreach, in othersmindedness, in valuing others about ourselves, in seeking the outsider, in doing something outside of what we would prefer.

What if the most controversial things Jesus spoke give us exactly what we need to remedy our Americanized caricature of the Savior? What if the demands he made wreck our lives in the best way possible? And what if that life is actually the life God intended for us - and the place where true joy is found? In this series, we are going to explore the most shocking things Jesus spoke and what they reveal about the Kingdom he came to establish. And not as outsiders interested in making Jesus some sort of rebel to admire from a distance. But as men and women who trust that even when his words disturb us, they are for our good. And they actually give us the life weâre all looking for.

The second part of May was back in beautiful Ohio, where I got to take more walks in the woods at the end of my street (6). I had a few different opportunities to learn about Northeast Ohio history at the James A Garfield National Historic Site (7) and the Perkins Stone Mansion (8). A new ice cream shop called Good Golly opened up in downtown Kent, with my favorite 18-year-old on their staff (9). And Iâve gotten to worship in a natural sanctuary formed by 300-year-old oak trees with H2O Church (10). But just so I donât paint too rosy a picture, I couldnât find images to show the frustrations of getting gouged by international rental vehicle agenciesâ¦ or the need to wear a puffer-coat with its waterproof shell for most of early-May in the United Kingdomâ¦ or my allergic reaction to the oak catkins in Ohio. Not that Iâm complaining. Lifeâs pretty good, but itâs also good to remember that highlight-reel images on a screen can only show certain things.

We look at how a 53-man roster of NFL players from Ohio State would stack up in 2026, including a seven-deep stable of No. 1 wide receivers and a star-studded defense.

â¢ Because NFL regular-season rosters are limited to 53 players, the All-Buckeye Team roster is, too. Thatâs why some active NFL players from Ohio State arenât on the team, though weâve also put together a practice squad with 16 of the top NFL Buckeyes that didnât make the 53-man roster.

â¢ To be eligible for the All-Buckeye Team, a player must either currently be on an active NFL roster or be an unretired free agent who played in at least one regular-season game in 2025.

â¢ The depth chart and roster were built as if we were an NFL GM trying to build the best possible team to win a Super Bowl in 2026; itâs not a career achievement award, so players on the back ends of their careers were not guaranteed starting jobs or roster spots based on past accomplishments.

â¢ There is no salary cap for the All-Buckeye Team.

â¢ Only players who finished their college careers at Ohio State are eligible for the All-Buckeye team, so you wonât find former Buckeyes who transferred elsewhere like Joe Burrow or Jameson Williams.

â¢ The All-Buckeye team will utilize the same base defensive structure as Ohio State: a 4-2-5 with two defensive ends, two defensive tackles, two linebackers, two cornerbacks and three safeties.

There are wide receivers who make plays and there are wide receivers who change games and then there is Jeremiah Smith â a category that does not have a proper name yet because the sport has not produced enough players like him to need one. The Apopka, Florida native arrived at Ohio State as the most talked about receiver prospect in years and then proceeded to do something that almost never happens at that level â he lived up to every single word of it from the very first game he played.
â
What separates Smith from every other elite receiver in college football is the combination of things he does that individually would make someone special and collectively make him something else entirely. The size at 6â3â that allows him to win contested catches over any corner in the country. The speed that creates separation before the route is even finished. The hands that make difficult catches look routine. And underneath all of it an understanding of leverage and positioning that most receivers do not develop until their third or fourth year in a system. Jeremiah Smith had it as a true freshman.
â
The numbers, the touchdowns, the highlight catches â all of it matters. But what truly defines what Jeremiah Smith is as a player is the way opposing defensive coordinators have to build their entire weekly game plan around the reality that he cannot be covered one on one by anyone on their roster. That is the most honest and most telling measure of a receiverâs impact at this level. When a defense changes what it does fundamentally because of one player and that player still finds a way to make plays anyway â that is when you know you are watching something genuinely rare.ââââââââââââââââ

Looking at the last month of my camera roll, I noticed that I had a lot of pictures of flowers. Iâll only share a snapshot of my first sighting of a crocus bloom (1), but the daffodils, hyacinths, and tulips have all been a thrill to see, as well!

In addition to flowers, I had a lot of pictures from the last month (Womenâs History Month!) that featured some pretty wonderful women, including a run in the Cuyahoga Valley with my sister Anna on the 20th (2)â¦ a lunch at Wild Goats Cafe, with my daughter Olivia serving as my hostess (3)â¦ girly drinks with my wife Marci, my daughter Olivia, and our friend Kelsey (4)â¦ and a family brunch that included my Mom Jan and my Aunt Jayne (5)!

In between all of the flowers and fun with the female members of my family (and friends), I got to support some strategic ministry initiatives here in Northeast Ohio. H2O Kentâs Rooted & Ready Spring Break trip (6) was especially noteworthy. But the âeverydayâ and weekly ministry stuff was meaningful, too, like the North Campus Life Group in Kent (7)â¦ and supervising this semesterâs two H2O interns, Trent and Noah (8).

And last but not least, March also provided an opportunity to watch the Cavs beat the Pistons with my sons Elliot and Cor (9)â¦ plus a family celebration of Elliotâs 24th birthday â including rhubarb pie and prayers for his life to blossom in the coming year much like weâre currently seeing with the crocuses, daffodils, hyacinths, and tulips. It really does feel like a miracle, every spring, that things which have seemed so dead and lifeless could be resurrected. But thatâs exactly what the Bible says is true for us: âjust as Christ was raised from the dead by the glorious power of the Father, now we also may live new lives!â I sincerely hope that you all have a Happy Easter!

Proverbs 3:5-7 tells us not to lean on our own understanding because our understanding is limited. Our vision is short. Our control is an illusion.

Jesus? He already won.

Through the Cross and the Resurrection, He defeated sin, conquered death, and secured our salvation. That means we donât trust God hoping He might come through. We trust Him because He already has.

So we humble ourselves.
We turn from self-reliance.

And we walk forward in confidence because Christ is victorious.

Trust Him fully.
Jesus already won.

To express endurance and forward momentum, I usedÂ motion-blurred imagery of a runner and feetÂ in different iterations, along with layered, fading typography to create a sense of movement. In any event, Iâm very thankful that we still have plenty of opportunities to experience âhomeâ and âfamilyâ in different forms, too (8-10). I hope youâre all hanging in there for the holidays!

label_values.value:
Rest in God as He rests in us.
â¢
This phrase is something that has been on my heart from the Lord so consistently. Rest in Him as He rests in us. Phew. Itâs simple but the truth. My life has been chaos recently, but not the chaos youâre imagining. Itâs a chaos that has been full of beautiful moments and opportunities, but yet God still tells me, âRest in me as I rest in you.â See, in the midst of this chaos, I started to feel overwhelmed, stressed, and anxious. I would come to God saying, âGod, why am I feeling this way? Why, when Iâm doing all of these things in Your name, do I start facing these emotions not of You?â I was doing things for God but not resting in His presence in the secret place.

He calls us to be with Him and know Him. When we seek Him, we know His heart (Jeremiah 29:13). When we know His heart, we experience His fruit (Galatians 5:22-23). When we experience His fruit, we proclaim it (Matthew 28:19-20). However, we canât continue to pour out when our cup is empty. Yes, reach your neighbor for Jesus. Yes, reach the lost so they can be found. Yes, do all these things in Godâs name, but itâs all useless if we arenât seeking His face on our own. For it says in Scripture, many will claim to have prophesied, driven out demons, and performed miracles all in Godâs name, but yet God will still say, âI never knew youâ (Matthew 7:22-23).

This shouldnât create a spirit of fear in us but be encouragement to seek Him daily. It should be encouragement to sit with Him in the secret place where thereâs no distraction, no people, nothing else but you and God. Heâs calling us to dine with Him, to laugh with Him, to share stories with Him, to do life with Him.

If youâve never accepted God into your heart, may this post be a sign. God wants you back. Your Creator, who knitted you in your motherâs womb, wants you back. He sees you exactly where you are and still calls you beloved. If you declare with your mouth that Jesus is Lord and believe in your heart that God raised Him from the dead, you will be saved (Romans 10:9). Jesus loves you so much. Seek Him today. â¤ï¸âð¥

We start up a new sermon series this Sunday at our 11am Worship Gathering titled âFaith in Actionâ which takes us through the book of James in the Bible. One of our designers, Hanna Crowe, designed this graphic - hereâs some of her inspiration behind it:

The collage focuses on the endurance of putting our faith into action, the refining trials we face, and the blessing that comes from enduring through trials.Â 

The main photo in the background is a foggy road, signifying the long and often unknown journey of our faith.

The flower in the corner signifies the blessing and beauty that lies on the other side of refinement, as well as the beauty of the eternity that awaits us with Jesus.Â 

The collage is overlaid with a photo of fire embers, signifying action, trials, and refinement.

âActionâ is glowing to signify the hope that we have during difficult trials and testing, how we keep our eyes on Jesus when everything seems foggy and difficult.

On Instagram, Carter regularly encourages his followers to trust God and boldly live for Jesus. His posts are less about highlights and more about pointing people toward faith.

âThe Gospel gives us purpose: to know God, to make Him known, to glorify Him, and to reflect Christ in the world,â Carter wrote in one post.

A standout at UConn, he became known for his toughness and versatility in the backfield before making his way to the NFL. Jesus Won // Fall Kickoff 

Christ Jesus holds such a presence in Columbus, OH. The Buckeyes are not only known for what they do on the field but also by their faith. Itâs truly amazing to see all the good God is doing. 

Such an amazing turnout last night, hundreds of people, top tier worship and an amazing Word. Buckeye Revival was everything imaginable and more. 

A huge shout out goes to former Ohio State TE and national champion Gee Scott Jr. he has The Holy Spirit working in him and through him. He was a big part in arranging last nights event and it was truly a pleasure meeting and working along side him. Towards the end of the night we had a conversation where he expressed how amazing it was that I was using my God given talent to document not only last nights event but the works of Christ. Thank you Jesus. Thank you to The Ohio State Football team and thank you to everyone who came or helped out with Buckeye Revival.

label_values.label: Caption
label_values.value:
âBut to all who did receive him, who believed in his name, he gave the right to become children of Godâ- John 1:12.

This summer, in the quiet of my room and in the everyday mundane moments, I started to learn what it looked like to be a daughter of God. My relationship with Jesus hasnât always been easy; for a while, there wasnât any love, at least not on my end. My relationship with my Savior was based off of fear, not love. I could never fully comprehend the fact that He truly loved me, and because of that, I would fear Him so much to the point of not even wanting to talk to Him. I would point to my faults and subconsciously say, âSee? How could you love me? No way.â I would ignore His love and just keep striving to prove myself, to try to earn His love in some way. I think this is because of the broken relationships that humans create; transactional relationships where love has to be earned. But this past school year and especially this summer, God has showed me that He is not the same. His love is not transactional in the way that we do not and absolutely cannot do anything to earn His love. It is something He freely gives, but it is up to us to accept it.

This can be difficult when we are dealing with shame from our past or guilt that keeps haunting us. How could God ever love me, knowing the things I have done? Yet He does. God so loved the world that He sent His only Son to come into the world, not to condemn it but to save it (John 3:16-17). He loved us yet while we were still sinners enough to die for us (Romans 5:8). He gives us the right to become His children when we believe in His name (John 1:12). God is a loving Father, waiting for you with open arms. He is love, He is merciful, and He loves us whether we accept it or not. But will you accept His love and allow that love to transform you from the inside out?

Remember the story of the prodigal son, a story of a man who runs from his father to live a life of sin. When returning home to his father, however, he is not met with condemnation, rather with love. The same is with God. His kindness and love is meant to lead us to repentance, so turn to Him today and let His love transform you forever.

God has been moving.
â¢
As I reflect on my first year of college, I canât help but stand in awe of all that God has done. Iâve witnessed people close to me step boldly into their callings in Jesus, using the unique gifts God has given them to share the true gospel with others. One of those people is my own mom. She has faithfully pursued her calling as an author and has been speaking at multiple womenâs events about her book, âHey Mom, Godâs Not Done With You Yet.â Seeing the doors God has opened for those around me has reminded me once again of the incredible ways He works through people of every age and background. Itâs been deeply inspiring and has only increased my awe of who God is and what He can do. When I began my journey at Kent, I didnât know exactly what to expectâbut I knew God had brought me there for a reason. I chose to dive in fully, trusting that He had something meaningful in store for me. Soon after arriving, I got involved in several amazing ministries and eventually found my home in two campus groups: H2O and Cru. At first, I was amazed by how many friends I made. But it didnât take long to realize they were becoming more than just friendsâthey were becoming family. Through these communities, Iâve had countless opportunities to share the gospel on campus through one-on-one evangelism, prayer circles, Bible studies, and so much more. I never could have imagined the ways God would choose to use me. But everything changed when I made the decision to stay open and willingâto be led by HIS HOLY SPIRIT, not by my own efforts or plans. So donât let your age, education, or background hold you back. If you are called, you are called (1 Timothy 4:12). And if youâre still breathing, that means God isnât done with you yet. I encourage you to take that next step of faith and see what He has for you. If you havenât already, join a community and grow alongside others. We were never meant to walk with the Lord aloneâwe are called to walk together (Ecclesiastes 4:9-12). I know God is stirring something powerful in this generationâIâve seen itâand He wants YOU to be a part of it.â¤ï¸âð¥

Easter Sunday. Jesus has risen and defeated death!!!

This is the best news that we could ever receive. That God, despite our sins and flaws, loved us so much that He sent His one and only son Jesus to die a painful death on a cross that only we could deserve. He took on the weight of all of our sins, took on the wrath of God that shouldâve been ours, and breathed His last. But it didnât end there!!! Three days later His tomb was found empty. He had risen, defeating death and the grave. Because of His resurrection, we can have both new life now and eternal life by putting our faith in Him and letting Him come into our lives, changing and transforming us from the inside out. Romans 10:9- âFor if you confess with your mouth that Jesus is Lord and believe in your heart that God raised Him from the dead, you will be saved.â Letting Jesus into my life was the best decision I couldâve ever made. When death was arrested, my life began!!! He waits for you, too, with open arms. He loves you so much, more than you could ever know, more than you could ever fathom. Jesus is alive. He is risen indeed.

Thank you Jesus. 

âBut the angel said to the women, âDo not be afraid, for I know that you seek Jesus who was crucified. He is not here, for he has risen, as he said.ââ Matthew 28:5ð

I can be thankful because each of them has shaped me into a better bride of Christ. I never could have imagined the abundance of beautiful people surrounding me, building me in my faith, or the evangelism opportunities Heâs given me to share my testimony with others. Most of all, I am grateful for the freedom He has shown me when we set our eyes completely on Him and nothing else.
I share all of this to say, God can do it. I am a living testimony. God will do it if you are willing and yielding to His Spirit. Even when it doesnât seem like it, He is right there with you every step of the way, carving a path for you. However, you must choose to walk His path, not your own. He sees you, loves you, and desires a relationship with you.
2025, here we comeâsurrendering our lives at Godâs feet. May we look to Jesus in all things and continue to find victory in our lives because of our obedience to Him.

label_values.value:
My end of the 2024 year post that no one asked forâ

a beautiful year. several highlights come to mind

- I spontaneously biked 16 miles from Kent to Akron university. I feel this is a memorable accomplishment.
- I had a wonderful roommate. And I had the privilege to see the literal start of her love story to then see her get married. I love being a bystander to those kind of things.
- I had the BEST 21st birthday. My friends made it so special. It was so nice to have everyone in one spot. Friends from different parts of my life meshed together. That brought me joy.
- I discovered that green tea and avocado toast gives me the best kick of happiness in the morning. 
- I learned that long walks, cooking, reading, exploring new places, and drinking coffee are my favorite things to do. 
- I love staying in. I specifically favor the nights of being planted on the couch with my very best friend while watching ridiculous dating shows. P.S. 95% of the couples do not make it out of the show.

This year really brought blessings and wisdom. I am SO thankful for the memories and growth. And I am incredibly thankful that I can go to bed knowing that I am a daughter of a King who crafted every aspect of me to enjoy these life-giving moments. While I can pick out which parts of my year that brought me the most joy and happiness, I have to look back at the true vessel of pure joy, peace, and happiness. Thank you for 2024.

-while life is moving way too fast, I have been trying to soak in all of the big and small moments that life has to offer. I feel that I have this pressure to really make senior year count and have no regrets. But, I am also starting to grieve my âcollege girlâ life as upcoming transitions are on the horizon. I have come to the realization that this grief is NORMAL, and there is no escaping it. There is joy in the fact that you grieve because of something that was good and brought you happiness.
